name: durnel
author: transport-maps-journeys
description:
durnel v2 (direction: transport, maps and journeys) - A ROAD WITH LOW BRIDGES AND LAY-BYS.
PRIVATE; never shown to players. v1 was too_easy (two Opus players 100 %/100 % WITHOUT a demo:
the rule was the famous lorry-vs-low-bridge fact and the edit was a guessable arrow swap, so they
enumerated rules offline against the "n turn" checksum, hit 81/81 on the first sensible rule and
never played a training probe). v2 keeps the checksum caption, the object, the kid reading and the
verb, and moves the difficulty into the EDIT and into one extra physical clause (fennick shape:
the picture says WHAT changes, only a demo says HOW).

CLUE = THE ROAD DRAWN FROM THE SIDE, plus one caption line "<n> turn".
  4-6 picture rows (blank rows above the tallest thing are trimmed), then a line of "=" as wide as
  the picture (the tarmac), then the caption "<n> turn". Width 60-73 columns, clue 260-519 chars.
  bottom picture row = the ground: "." open road, "\_/" a LAY-BY (exactly 3 columns), a lorry
  occupying exactly three columns.
  A LORRY of height h is a solid block of its own capital letter, three columns wide and h rows
  tall, standing on the ground row; its NOSE replaces one end of its bottom row: "TT>" faces right,
  "<TT" faces left. Heights 1..M-1 are uniform-random and GIVEN by the drawing - there is no height
  formula to hunt. 6-7 lorries, 4 beams, 4 lay-bys.
  A BRIDGE is a beam of 3-4 "#" at one row; the free rows between the beam and the ground row are
  its CLEARANCE k (2..M-2). Beams, lay-bys and lorries NEVER share a column (>=1 blank column
  between every drawn item) and both ends of the road are open tarmac. Load-bearing: a lorry's
  height is simply the non-blank cells of its middle column, a lay-by is found with one find('_'),
  and the range "between the lorry and the lay-by" can be sliced without excluding their own
  columns (they carry no beam). Do not relax it.

ANSWER = THE CLUE'S PICTURE WITH EVERY TURNING LORRY REDRAWN IN ITS LAY-BY, FACING BACK.
A turning lorry is erased from where it stood (those three columns become plain road ".") and
redrawn, same letter, same height, in the three columns of the lay-by, with its nose at the other
end ("LL>" driving right becomes "<LL" sitting in the lay-by). Nothing else changes: same rows,
same beams, same tarmac, same letters. The answer is UNIQUE per clue (no two lorries ever want the
same lay-by - generation rejects that). The trailing "<n> turn" line may be kept or dropped; both
score 1 (house rule 2026-09-05).

RULE (one clause): A LORRY TURNS ROUND IN THE FIRST LAY-BY IT COMES TO, IF THERE IS A BRIDGE
FURTHER ON THAT WAY THAT IT CANNOT FIT UNDER. Said in one breath: "there's a bridge ahead it can't
get under, so it pulls into the first lay-by and turns round". Two things fall out of the physics
and are the whole difficulty: (a) if the bridge it cannot fit under comes BEFORE any lay-by, it
never reaches one - it just stops, and NOTHING in the picture changes (the famous fact alone
therefore over-counts, and the offline checksum falsifies it); (b) "cannot fit" is strict -
clearance < height, so a lorry exactly as tall as the clearance drives through. It is a JOURNEY
rule: the whole road ahead on the side the nose points counts, the road behind counts for nothing.

WHY v2 IS NOT v1. The blind reading of v1 (famous fact + swap the nose where it stands) scores
0.0 % here: it neither picks the right lorries nor renders a legal edit. A blind player who does
enumerate rules against the caption is stopped one step earlier than in v1 - "too tall for a bridge
ahead" does NOT reproduce n (every clue plants a lorry that is blocked with no lay-by in front of
it), so the first sensible rule is falsified rather than confirmed 81/81. And even a player who
guesses the selection cannot verify a RENDERING offline: the caption says how many turn, not where
they end up. With the demo the caption is a full checksum again (100 % of clues).

EVERY DEMO TEACHES THE WHOLE RULE. generate() plants, in every instance (audited over 4000 clues):
  P5  a lorry blocked by a bridge with NO lay-by in front of it -> it does not move          100 %
      (87.9 % of clues also have its lay-by drawn just PAST the blocking bridge, which kills
      "blocked ahead, move to your nearest lay-by" as well as the plain famous fact)
  P1  a turner that drives UNDER an earlier bridge and is stopped by a later one             100 %
      -> kills "only the next bridge counts"
  P7  a turner that drives PAST a second lay-by -> it takes the FIRST one, not the last      100 %
  P3  a lorry a bridge exactly its own height would stop -> kills "<=" instead of "<"        100 %
  P2  a lorry that would turn if it faced the other way -> kills the mirrored rule           100 %
  P4  a stander with a lay-by ahead and a bridge beyond it that it fits under                100 %
      -> kills "a lay-by and a bridge ahead is enough"
  P6  a standing lorry TALLER than a turning one -> kills "the n tallest turn"               100 %
  and, when n>=2, turners facing both ways and standers facing both ways (100 %).
The demo is a picture pair; the diff is n lorries that have left their place and are sitting in a
lay-by facing back, with the road they left drawn as plain dots.

THE FOOTHOLD (lever 7). 12.2 % of clues say "0 turn": nothing turns and the correct answer IS the
clue returned unchanged, caption kept or dropped. A demo-less player who reads "a road, lorries,
bridges, lay-bys, 2 turn" off the clue and echoes the picture scores ~12 %, and so does every
count-based guess. Unlike v1, a demo-less player who applies the famous fact scores 0.0 %, because
the answer's shape (a lorry moves) is not guessable - which is exactly why a team should spend a
demo here rather than on a class whose edit is obvious.

WITNESS TABLE (1500 fresh clues, shipped scorer. Templates render with the TRUE drawing convention,
i.e. a player who has seen a demo and holds the wrong rule; the two BLIND lines model a player who
has not):
  BLIND: famous fact + v1's edit (nose swapped in place)     0.0 %   <- was 100 % in v1
  BLIND: famous fact + a lay-by ahead, nose swapped in place  1.1 %
  clue returned unchanged                                   12.1 %   <- the foothold
  clue unchanged, caption dropped                           12.1 %
  famous fact, rendered as a move into the first lay-by     12.5 %
  true rule, moved but not turned round                     12.1 %
  true rule, turned round on the spot (no move)             12.1 %
  true rule, into the LAST lay-by before the bridge         12.1 %
  an equal-height bridge blocks too (<= instead of <)        0.0 %
  a lorry can squeeze under a bridge one row too low        15.2 %
  only the NEXT bridge ahead counts                         12.1 %
  only the first bridge PAST the lay-by counts               9.5 %
  mirrored: look behind instead of ahead                     0.0 %
  any too-low bridge anywhere (direction ignored)            3.2 %
  a lorry ahead stops you too                               12.5 %
  a lorry coming the other way stops you                    10.5 %
  a lay-by then ANY bridge ahead (heights ignored)           0.0 %
  every lorry with a lay-by ahead                            0.0 %
  the n tallest / n shortest lorries                        12.1 / 12.3 %
  the first n lorries, left to right                        14.2 %
  n random lorries                                          17.0 %   <- the top rival
  each lorry moves with probability 1/2                      3.3 %
  every lorry turns its nose round                           0.0 %
  true rule, vacated slot blanked with spaces               12.1 %
  true rule, lorry copied into the lay-by (not moved)       12.1 %
  caption forced to 0 turn                                  12.1 %
  demo replay (another clue's answer)                        0.0 %
  junk / empty / half the picture / the caption / 4000 chars 0.0 %
  TRUE RULE (solve), caption kept / dropped / rows padded  100.0 %
No template exceeds 17 %, and everything at ~12 % is really just the "0 turn" foothold. The class is
therefore demo-or-foothold by design (fennick's profile): the split between the two players in a
pool comes from who spends a demo here, not from who probes harder.

WELL-FORMEDNESS (20 hand-built attacks, 600 clues each, all 0.0 % unless noted): no tarmac row, two
tarmac rows, tarmac of dashes, tarmac one column short, a blank row added on top, picture rows
reversed, the picture mirrored left-right, every nose flipped on top of the answer, letters
lowercased, beams erased, lay-bys erased, the caption's count changed, the answer plus a junk line,
4000 chars of junk, noses replaced by "v", road dots replaced by spaces, the caption alone, the
empty string. Declared leniencies (100 %): trailing newlines, trailing whitespace on any row, and
the caption line present or absent. The scorer rebuilds the whole expected picture from the clue
and compares it row by row, so nothing about the rule can be smuggled through them.

ENGINEERING (4000 fresh seeds). generate mean 0.83 ms, p99 3.6 ms, max 5.0 ms, 0 fallback uses,
3000/3000 clues distinct and deterministic; solve mean 0.037 ms; score mean 0.037 ms on real
answers and 0.036 ms on junk (including 4000-char junk); scorer 506/512 chars, solve 1492, clue
260-519 chars, solution 260-519 chars, 1500/1500 answers distinct. n is 0 (12.2 %) or 2-4; the
turning set is never the tallest, the shortest or the first n lorries.

INTENDED SPLIT. With a demo: the two pictures differ by whole lorries that have moved into lay-bys
and turned round, so the rendering is read in one look; the remaining question, "why those?", has
the everyday answer, and the caption then verifies any candidate rule offline against ~70 harvested
clues (100 % on the true rule, and the near-miss plants make every close rule fail). Two rounds of
~60 probes are enough to confirm. Without a demo: the clue is a drawn road with a verb and a count,
so echoing it banks the ~12 % zero cases, but the famous fact scores 0 %, because the edit moves a
lorry across the picture and no blind reading produces that.

LEVERS. Too easy: (a) require the caption dropped, which removes the identity foothold and the
offline checksum; (b) let a beam sit directly over a lorry so the height read costs a probe;
(c) make a lorry that is stopped short of every lay-by reverse to the open end of the road instead
of standing still. Too hard: (a) draw one lorry already sitting in a lay-by in the clue as a worked
instance; (b) drop the nose flip, so the edit is only "it moves into the lay-by"; (c) guarantee
exactly one lay-by before every blocking bridge, which removes the first-vs-last question.
generate:
# A ROAD WITH LOW BRIDGES AND LAY-BYS. Lorries (3 columns wide, h rows tall, a nose
# ">" or "<" on the bottom row) stand on the road; "#" beams cross overhead; a lay-by is
# drawn "\_/" in the road. A lorry that meets a beam it cannot fit under turns round --
# but only if it passed a lay-by first: it is redrawn there, facing back. Every clue
# plants the near-misses (see description); ~12 % of clues say "0 turn".
FB = ("             CCC                 SSS ###              ###\n"
      " ###         CCC LLL      ####   SSS                      HHH\n"
      "             CCC LLL             SSS                      HHH\n"
      "     GGG     CCC LLL             SSS                      HHH\n"
      ".....<GG.JJ>.<CC.LL>.\\_/.........<SS.....\\_/.\\_/..\\_/.....<HH.\n"
      "==============================================================\n"
      "2 turn")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    AL = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVW"
    K = 99                                        # "no such item ahead"
    zero = r.random() < 0.12                      # decided once, before any retry
    for att in range(300):
        M = r.randint(6, 7)                       # picture rows; max lorry height M-1
        hm = M - 1
        nL = r.randint(6, 7)
        seq = ["L"] * nL + ["B"] * 4 + ["Y"] * 4
        r.shuffle(seq)
        wid = [3 if t != "B" else r.choice((3, 4)) for t in seq]
        k = len(seq)
        gaps = [1] * (k + 1)                      # >=1 blank column between drawn items
        for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
            gaps[r.randrange(k + 1)] += 1
        W = sum(wid) + sum(gaps)
        pos = []
        x = gaps[0]
        for i, (t, w) in enumerate(zip(seq, wid)):
            pos.append((t, x, w))
            x += w + gaps[i + 1]
        cl = [r.randint(2, M - 2) if t == "B" else 0 for t, _, _ in pos]
        Ls = [i for i, p in enumerate(pos) if p[0] == "L"]

        BAY, BEAM, FB_, FLE = {}, {}, {}, {}
        for i in Ls:
            for d in (1, -1):
                A = [(seq[j], cl[j]) for j in (range(i + 1, k) if d > 0 else range(i - 1, -1, -1))]
                BAY[i, d] = [u for u, (t, c) in enumerate(A) if t == "Y"]
                BEAM[i, d] = bm = [(u, c) for u, (t, c) in enumerate(A) if t == "B"]
                # first bridge ahead too low for a lorry of height h (K = none)
                FB_[i, d] = [min([u for u, c in bm if c < h] + [K]) for h in range(hm + 2)]
                FLE[i, d] = [min([u for u, c in bm if c <= h] + [K]) for h in range(hm + 2)]

        OPT = {}
        for i in Ls:
            for d in (1, -1):
                bays, bm, fb, fle = BAY[i, d], BEAM[i, d], FB_[i, d], FLE[i, d]
                b1 = bays[0] if bays else K
                u0 = bm[0][0] if bm else K
                ul = bm[-1][0] if bm else -1
                nb2 = [len([u for u in bays if u < f]) > 1 for f in fb]
                rb = BAY[i, -d]
                b2 = rb[0] if rb else K
                rf = FB_[i, -d]
                for h in range(1, hm + 1):
                    f = fb[h]
                    t = b1 < f < K
                    F = set()
                    if t:
                        F.add("T")
                        if u0 < f:
                            F.add("P1")           # it drives under an earlier bridge first
                        if nb2[h]:
                            F.add("P7")           # it drove past a second lay-by
                    else:
                        if f < b1:
                            F.add("P5")           # stopped before it reached a lay-by
                        if ul > b1:
                            F.add("P4")           # a lay-by, then a bridge it fits under
                    if (b1 < fle[h] < K) != t:
                        F.add("P3")               # "an equal bridge blocks too" would differ
                    if (b2 < rf[h] < K) != t:
                        F.add("P2")               # "look behind you" would differ
                    OPT[i, d, h] = F

        need = ["P5", "P3", "P2", "P4"] if zero else ["P5", "P1", "P3", "P2", "P4"]
        H, D, got = {}, {}, set()
        order = Ls[:]
        r.shuffle(order)
        ok = 1
        for role in need:
            if role in got:
                continue
            done = 0
            for i in order:
                if i in H:
                    continue
                ch = [(d, h) for d in (1, -1) for h in range(1, hm + 1)
                      if role in OPT[i, d, h] and not (zero and "T" in OPT[i, d, h])]
                if ch:
                    d, h = r.choice(ch)
                    H[i] = h; D[i] = d; got |= OPT[i, d, h]; done = 1
                    break
            if not done:
                ok = 0
                break
        if not ok:
            continue
        H0, D0 = dict(H), dict(D)
        free = [i for i in Ls if i not in H0]
        CT = {i: [(d, h) for d in (1, -1) for h in range(1, hm + 1) if "T" in OPT[i, d, h]] for i in free}
        CS = {i: [(d, h) for d in (1, -1) for h in range(1, hm + 1) if "T" not in OPT[i, d, h]] for i in free}
        F = sum("T" in OPT[i, D0[i], H0[i]] for i in H0)
        mustT = [i for i in free if not CS[i]]
        optT = [i for i in free if CS[i] and CT[i]]
        base = F + len(mustT)
        lo, hi = (0, 0) if zero else (max(2, base), min(4, base + len(optT)))
        if lo > hi or (zero and base):
            continue
        best = None
        for a in range(12):
            H, D = dict(H0), dict(D0)
            nt = r.randint(lo, hi)
            turners = mustT + r.sample(optT, nt - base)
            for i in free:
                D[i], H[i] = r.choice(CT[i] if i in turners else CS[i])
            T = [i for i in Ls if "T" in OPT[i, D[i], H[i]]]
            S = [i for i in Ls if i not in T]
            n = len(T)
            if n != nt:
                continue
            if len(S) > 1 and {D[i] for i in S} != {1, -1}:
                continue
            if n > 1 and {D[i] for i in T} != {1, -1}:
                continue
            if n and max(H[i] for i in S) <= min(H[i] for i in T):
                continue                          # a stander must be taller than a turner
            bay = [i + (1 + BAY[i, D[i]][0]) * D[i] for i in T]
            if len(set(bay)) < n:
                continue                          # two lorries wanting the same lay-by
            if att < 240 and not (zero or any("P7" in OPT[i, D[i], H[i]] for i in T)):
                continue     # one turner must drive PAST a lay-by: it takes the FIRST one
            best = (dict(H), dict(D), n)
            break
        if not best:
            continue
        H, D, n = best
        letters = r.sample(AL, nL)
        P = [[" "] * W for _ in range(M)]
        P[M - 1] = ["."] * W
        for u, i in enumerate(Ls):
            t, x0, w = pos[i]
            c = letters[u]
            for v in range(H[i]):
                P[M - 1 - v][x0:x0 + 3] = [c] * 3
            P[M - 1][x0 + (2 if D[i] > 0 else 0)] = ">" if D[i] > 0 else "<"
        for i, (t, x0, w) in enumerate(pos):
            if t == "B":
                P[M - 1 - cl[i]][x0:x0 + w] = ["#"] * w
            elif t == "Y":
                P[M - 1][x0:x0 + 3] = ["\\", "_", "/"]
        Q = ["".join(y).rstrip() for y in P]
        while Q and not Q[0]:
            Q.pop(0)                              # no blank rows above the tallest thing
        return "\n".join(Q) + "\n" + "=" * W + "\n" + str(n) + " turn"
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    P = clue.split("\n")
    T = P.pop()                                   # the "<n> turn" caption, copied through
    B = P.pop()                                   # the tarmac
    W = len(B)
    L = P[-1]                                     # the ground row: road, lay-bys, lorries
    Z = ["".join(z) for z in zip(*[z.ljust(W) for z in P])]    # read column by column
    A = [z.rfind("#") for z in Z]                 # row of the lowest beam over each column
    E = Z[:]
    for m in re.finditer("<..|..>", L):
        j = m.start()
        b = Z[j + 1]                              # the lorry's middle column
        g = b.count(" ")                          # blank rows above it: a beam at row >= g hits it
        k = m[0] < "A"                            # is it facing left?
        p = L.rfind("_", 0, j) if k else L.find("_", j)        # the first lay-by ahead
        if p < 0:
            continue
        near = A[p:j] + A[j:p]                    # between the lorry and that lay-by
        far = A[:p] if k else A[p:]               # everything beyond the lay-by
        if max(near + [-1]) < g <= max(far + [-1]):
            # it turns round in the lay-by: redrawn there, facing back the other way
            E[p - 1:p + 2] = [b] * 3
            E[p - 1 + 2 * k] = b[:-1] + "<>"[k]
            E[j:j + 3] = [Z[0]] * 3               # its old place is open road again
    return "\n".join(z.rstrip() for z in map("".join, zip(*E))) + "\n" + B + "\n" + T
